analyst_view.overall: Early view: Galatasaray (18th, 6 points) beat Stuttgart 2-0 on matchday 4 with two early goals from Alexey Batrakov, while Aston Villa lost their perfect record with a 3-0 defeat in Barcelona and then drew 4-4 at Manchester United. Villa have conceded seven goals in two games and Unai Emery stormed off the touchline at Old Trafford, so the visitors arrive less settled than their 6th place suggests; Emery is in talks over a new contract, so his position itself is not in question.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals and I lean a little higher. Villa have just conceded three at Barcelona and four at Old Trafford, plus a late Fulham equaliser from a Zion Suzuki error, while Galatasaray scored twice in 15 minutes against Stuttgart. Galatasaray started fast against Stuttgart, and Villa's defence is the weak point right now.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners and I have nothing that moves it much. Galatasaray scored early against Stuttgart and then sat on the lead, which limits their corner count, and Villa were outplayed in Barcelona. A fairly even split of around nine looks right.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards and I lean higher. Galatasaray's game with Stuttgart produced eight yellow cards, and Villa collected three in the first half alone in Barcelona (Ian Maatsen, Emiliano Buendia, Nicolas Jackson). A loud Istanbul crowd and a side under pressure points to a busy night for the referee.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots and I stay close to it. Galatasaray scored twice early against Stuttgart and Villa's recent games have been open, with eight goals at Old Trafford. Nothing I found argues for a big move either way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target. Villa's leaky defence argues for more Galatasaray efforts on goal, but Villa's own attack was shut out in Barcelona, so the two effects roughly cancel. I stay with the estimate.
